newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian opposition activist freed, another held.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian opposition activist freed, another held.

text.p: A leading member of the Nigerian opposition has been freed from detention after two years without trial and another arrested, local papers reported on Thursday.

They said secretary of the National Democratic Coalition (NADECO) group Ayo Opadokun, 50, was freed from a prison in the capital Abuja on Wednesday while Doyin Okupe, a member of NADECO was arrested in Lagos.

There was no official confirmation of either development but Opadokun was quoted by the independent National Concord newspaper as saying in Abuja: "The deputy controller of prisons just called me to inform me that my release order has come."

Opadokun was detained in October 1994 after the government crushed strikes and riots in southwestern Nigeria pressing for the release and installation as president of Moshood Abiola, who is widely believed to have won an annulled 1993 election.

In June Nigeria freed half a dozen detainees to coincide with its first meeting with the Commonwealth from which the West African country was suspended last November after the hanging of nine minority rights activists for murder.
Despite the recent releases, many people remain in detention, chiefly Abiola and several pro-democracy activists.
